Subject: Moving to Trunk-Based Development

## The problem

Our long-lived feature branches routinely live for two to four weeks before merging. By the time they land, they've drifted so far from main that integration becomes its own multi-day project. Over the last quarter this has shown up as: merge conflicts that eat entire afternoons, "integration hell" weeks where three branches land at once and something breaks, and QA finding bugs that are actually the product of two branches interacting badly, not either branch alone. We're twelve engineers, which means at any given time we can have six or more branches diverging simultaneously. The bigger the branch, the bigger the blast radius when it finally merges, and the harder it is to tell which change caused a regression.

## The proposal

- Merge to main at least once a day, per developer, using small commits.
- Gate incomplete work behind feature flags instead of behind a branch, so main stays releasable at all times.
- Require CI (tests + linting) to pass on every merge to main, with a fast pipeline (under 10 minutes) so this isn't a bottleneck.
- Break large features into a sequence of small, independently mergeable pull requests reviewed within hours, not days.
- Run a two-week pilot with one squad before rolling out team-wide, so we can fix workflow issues before they hit everyone.

## What could go wrong

The strongest objection is that trunk-based development can expose half-finished work to the rest of the team and, if flags are managed sloppily, to production. A mis-set flag or a stale one left in code is a real risk, and it's fair to worry that this trades merge-day pain for scattered, harder-to-trace incidents. I don't think this risk disappears — it has to be managed with flag hygiene reviews and a "no flag lives past one release" rule, plus rollback drills. There's also real short-term cost: engineers used to branch autonomy will feel exposed working in the open, and our review process needs to speed up or PRs will queue up against daily-merge expectations.

I would like a decision by the end of next week.
